entries.title: Acts 24:1
segments: ¶Now after five days Ananias the high priest came down with the elders and a certain orator [named] Tertullus. These gave evidence to the governor against Paul.

entries.title: Acts 24:2
segments: And when he was called upon, Tertullus began his accusation, saying: "Seeing that through you we enjoy great peace, and prosperity is being brought to this nation by your foresight,

entries.title: Acts 24:3
segments: "we accept [it] always and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.

entries.title: Acts 24:4
segments: "Nevertheless, not to be tedious to you any further, I beg you to hear, by your courtesy, a few words from us.

entries.title: Acts 24:5
segments: "For we have found this man a plague, a creator of dissension among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.

entries.title: Acts 24:6
segments: "He even tried to profane the temple, and we seized him, and wanted to judge him according to our law.

entries.title: Acts 24:7
segments: "But the commander Lysias came by and with great violence took [him] out of our hands,

entries.title: Acts 24:8
segments: "commanding his accusers to come to you. By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him."

entries.title: Acts 24:9
segments: And the Jews also assented, maintaining that these things were so.

entries.title: Acts 24:10
segments: ¶Then Paul, after the governor had nodded to him to speak, answered: "Inasmuch as I know that you have been for many years a judge of this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself,

entries.title: Acts 24:11
segments: "because you may ascertain that it is no more than twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

entries.title: Acts 24:12
segments: "And they neither found me in the temple disputing with anyone nor inciting the crowd, either in the synagogues or in the city.

entries.title: Acts 24:13
segments: "Nor can they prove the things of which they now accuse me.

entries.title: Acts 24:14
segments: "But this I confess to you, that according to the Way which they call a sect, so I worship the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the Law and in the Prophets.

entries.title: Acts 24:15
segments: "I have hope in God, which they themselves also accept, that there will be a resurrection of [the] dead, both of [the] just and [the] unjust.

entries.title: Acts 24:16
segments: "This [being] so, I myself always strive to have a conscience without offense toward God and men.

entries.title: Acts 24:17
segments: "Now after many years I came to bring alms and offerings to my nation,

entries.title: Acts 24:18
segments: "in the midst of which some Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with a mob nor with tumult.

entries.title: Acts 24:19
segments: "They ought to have been here before you to object if they had anything against me.

entries.title: Acts 24:20
segments: "Or else let those who are [here] themselves say if they found any wrongdoing in me while I stood before the council,

entries.title: Acts 24:21
segments: "unless [it is] for this one statement which I cried out, standing among them, 'Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged by you this day.'"

entries.title: Acts 24:22
segments: ¶But when Felix heard these things, having more accurate knowledge of [the] Way, he adjourned the proceedings and said, "When Lysias the commander comes down, I will make a decision on your case."

entries.title: Acts 24:23
segments: So he commanded the centurion to keep Paul and to let [him] have liberty, and told him not to forbid any of his friends to provide for or visit him.

entries.title: Acts 24:24
segments: And after some days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, he sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

entries.title: Acts 24:25
segments: Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, "Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you."

entries.title: Acts 24:26
segments: Meanwhile he also hoped that money would be given him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore he sent for him more often and conversed with him.

entries.title: Acts 24:27
segments: But after two years Porcius Festus succeeded Felix; and Felix, wanting to do the Jews a favor, left Paul bound.
